nodes.label: Natural Gas in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Clean energy source. KG basin, Mumbai High, Cambay basin, Assam, Rajasthan. Used in power, fertiliser, petrochemical industries. CNG for urban transport. Growing share in energy mix.

nodes.label: Manufacturing in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Secondary sector activity. Contributes about 17% to GDP (needs to increase to 25%). Employs about 12% of workforce. Important for modernisation and poverty reduction. Classified by size, raw material, ownership.

nodes.label: Automobile Industry
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Rapid growth after liberalisation. India emerging as major manufacturer. Delhi, Gurgaon, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Lucknow, Jamshedpur, Bangalore major centres. Both commercial and passenger vehicles.

nodes.label: National Manufacturing Policy
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Aims to increase manufacturing share in GDP to 25% and create 100 million jobs. National Investment and Manufacturing Zones. Make in India initiative to promote manufacturing. Skill development focus.

nodes.label: Industrial Agglomeration
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Industries cluster for shared infrastructure, labour pool, market access, ancillary support. Results in industrial regions. Mumbai-Pune, Delhi-NCR, Chennai corridor are examples. Causes regional concentration.

nodes.label: Cottage and Small Industries
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Important for employment, especially rural. Khadi and Village Industries Commission promotes them. Include handicrafts, handlooms, food processing. Government reservations and financial support.

nodes.label: Pipelines in India
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Network of 15000+ km for crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas. HBJ (Hazira-Bijaipur-Jagdishpur) pipeline for gas. Reduces dependence on rail/road transport for energy. Cheap for transporting liquids.

nodes.label: Iron and Steel Industry
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Basic industry. Crescent region (Chhattisgarh, Orissa, Jharkhand, WB). TISCO Jamshedpur, Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro, Vizag. SAIL manages public plants.

nodes.label: Cotton Textile Industry
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: First mill 1854 Mumbai. 1782 mills (1998). Powerloom 59%, handloom 19%, mill 6%. Maharashtra, Gujarat, TN lead. TN most mills. Swadeshi impetus.

nodes.label: Sugar Industry
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Second agro-based. Largest sugarcane/cane sugar producer (8% world). Seasonal. Maharashtra 1/3 (119 mills). UP second. Crush within 24 hours.

nodes.label: Industrial Location Factors
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Raw materials, power, market, transport, labour, capital, history, policy. Weight-losing near raw materials. Market-oriented near consumers.

nodes.label: World Population Distribution
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: 90% in 10% of land. 10 most populous countries 60% (6 in Asia). Dense: NE USA, NW Europe, S/SE/E Asia. Sparse: polar, desert, equatorial.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Factors Influencing Distribution
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Geographical: water, landforms, climate, soils. Economic: minerals, urbanisation, industrialisation. Social/cultural: religious significance, stability.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Demographic Transition
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Three stages: I high birth/death (agrarian); II high birth/declining death (health improvement); III low birth/death (urban, industrial, literate).
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: World Population Growth
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Doubled 500M(1650) to 1B(1850) in 200yrs, then 4B(1975) in 125yrs. 80M added yearly. Developing countries most growth.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Components of Change
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Births (CBR), deaths (CDR), migration. Natural growth = births - deaths. Push factors (unemployment, disasters), pull factors (jobs).
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Doubling Time
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Reducing: 1500yrs(to 500M), 200yrs(to 1B), 80yrs(to 2B), 45yrs(to 4B). Developed take longer.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Malthusian Theory
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Population increases faster than food (1793). Excess leads to famine, disease, war. Preventive checks better.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Population Control
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Family planning. Propaganda, contraceptives, tax disincentives. India growth rate 1.9%, doubles in 36 years.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: HIV/AIDS Impact
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Deadly in Africa, CIS, Asia. Pushed up death rates, reduced life expectancy, slowed growth.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Spatial Pattern of Change
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Growth low in developed, high in developing. Negative correlation with economic development. Africa highest (2.6%), Europe near zero.
nodes.chapter_title: World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth

nodes.label: Terrace Farming
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Crops grown on terraces built on steep slopes to create flat surfaces. Prevents water from running off rapidly. Practised in mountains and hills of Ganga-Brahmaputra basin.
nodes.chapter_title: Human Environment Interactions: Tropical and Subtropical Region

nodes.label: Velds
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Temperate grasslands of South Africa. Rolling plateaus 600-1100m height. Bounded by Drakensberg Mountains (east) and Kalahari Desert (west). Drained by tributaries of Orange and Limpopo rivers.

nodes.label: Veld Climate
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Mild climate due to Indian Ocean influence. Cold dry winters (5-10C, July coldest). Short warm summers (about 20C). Rainfall mainly in summer (Nov-Feb) from warm ocean currents.

nodes.label: Veld Economy
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Known for cattle rearing and mining. Sheep rearing most important (Merino sheep for warm wool). Dairy farming significant. Rich mineral reserves. Johannesburg: gold capital. Kimberley: diamond mines.

nodes.label: Merino Sheep
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Popular sheep species in Velds bred mainly for wool. Wool is very warm and valuable, giving rise to wool industry in the velds.

nodes.label: Johannesburg
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Known as the gold capital of the world. Located in the Velds of South Africa. Mining of gold and diamond led to trade ties with Britain and South Africa becoming a British colony.

nodes.label: Ladakh Cold Desert
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Cold desert in Great Himalayas, eastern Jammu and Kashmir. Karakoram Range (north), Zanskar mountains (south). Altitude 3000m (Kargil) to 8000m+ (Karakoram). Indus is most important river. Gangri glacier.

nodes.label: Ladakh Climate
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Extremely cold and dry due to high altitude. Thin air makes sun felt intensely. Summer day temps just above 0C, winter below -40C. Rain shadow of Himalayas, only 10 cm rainfall/year. Drass is one of coldest inhabited places.

nodes.label: Ladakh Flora and Fauna
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Sparse vegetation: scanty grasses, willows, poplars in valleys. Summer fruits: apples, apricots, walnuts. Birds: robins, redstarts, Tibetan snowcock. Animals: wild goats, wild sheep, yak. Chiru (Tibetan antelope) endangered for shahtoosh wool.

nodes.label: Ladakh People and Culture
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Muslims and Buddhists. Buddhist monasteries (gompas): Hemis, Thiksey, Shey, Lamayuru. Grow barley, potatoes, peas in summer. Tourism major activity. NH 1A connects Leh to Kashmir through Zoji La Pass.

nodes.label: Wheat
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Requires moderate temperature and rainfall, bright sunshine at harvest. Thrives in well-drained loamy soil. Grown in USA, Canada, Argentina, Russia, Ukraine, Australia, India. Winter crop in India.

nodes.label: Population Explosion
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Rapid growth of world population especially after 1800. From 1 billion (1804) to 6 billion (1999). Caused by declining death rates while birth rates remained high. Better food supplies and medicine main reasons.
